newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico institute says market turbulence ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mexico institute says market turbulence ahead.

text.p: Mexican financial markets could be shaken by a speculative onslaught half-way through 1997 as mid-term elections approach, the private-sector-run Mexican Institute for Political Studies (IMEP) said on Wednesday.

"If the speculative onslaught is unleashed, it won't be so much the fault of the transition towards democracy (but rather because) Mexico is financially vulnerable," IMEP Research Coordinator Javier Gonzalez told journalists.

Mexicans will go to the polls on July 6 to renew the entire lower house of the Mexican Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, seven state governors, including the first ever election for Mexico City's mayor.
"As long as the country depends on short-term foreign capital for its growth...it will be financially and economically vulnerable," Gonzalez added.
